conclusion.justification: The report unequivocally states that hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19, citing large randomized trials and meta-analyses showing no benefit and potential harm.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
Based on the evidence from large randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses, the answer is **no** — hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19. Your sister's belief is not supported by the best available clinical evidence.

**Key evidence:**

1. **The RECOVERY Trial (UK):** This large randomized trial, published in the *New England Journal of Medicine*, found that hydroxychloroquine was no better than usual care at reducing death among hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The trial arm was halted because the drug showed no benefit. ([Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/health/anti-malaria-drug-hydroxychloroquine-ineffective-against-coronavirus-reveal-uk-recovery-trials-8896831.html); [Yahoo News](https://www.yahoo.com/news/uk-halts-trial-hydroxychloroquine-covid-140017966.html))

2. **The WHO Solidarity Trial:** This multinational trial across 30 countries found that hydroxychloroquine (along with lopinavir/ritonavir and interferon) had "little or no effect" on mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. WHO stopped the hydroxychloroquine arm in June 2020 based on accumulating evidence of futility. ([WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-hydroxychloroquine); [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa2023184))

3. **International Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials:** A 2021 meta-analysis published in *Nature Communications* pooled data from randomized trials and found that hydroxychloroquine was actually associated with **increased** mortality compared to control groups. ([Nature Communications](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z))

**Bottom line:** Multiple large, well-designed randomized trials and meta-analyses consistently show that hydroxychloroquine does not reduce COVID-19 mortality. Early observational studies and anecdotal reports suggested possible benefit, but these were less reliable and were not confirmed by rigorous randomized trials. The scientific consensus is clear: hydroxychloroquine should not be used to treat COVID-19.
